title: Steering wheel
prompt: A labelled teaching model combines the page 32 steering wheel with the page 43 unassisted rack-and-pinion steering linkage. Turn left and Turn right rotate the column pinion, move the rack and track rods, and swivel the two front-wheel steering arms. Compare wheel sizes exchanges two rim diameters while keeping the same steering linkage and road-wheel resisting load. It compares the tangential hand force needed for the same shaft torque. See-through exposes the rim, hub, column, pinion, rack, track rods and steering arms. Do not add a power-steering pump or motor.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / The Wheel and Axle
blurb: An unassisted steering model combines the book diagrams with exchangeable teaching rims to compare hand force at the same column torque and prescribed road resistance.

identity.note: The Wheel and Axle at Work / Steering Wheel, page 32. Gears and Belts / The Rack and Pinion / Car Steering, page 43 supplies the road-wheel linkage in both editions.
identity.mechanism: Rim effort turns the steering column. A pinion shifts a rack, track rods and steering arms swivel the front wheels. Wheel, rack-and-pinion and levers act together.
identity.classificationNote: Only The Wheel and Axle and Gears and Belts are main principle chapters in this unit. Other entries are named examples, diagrams or subsection headings. Greek Mill has both historical context and a named mechanism diagram.

adaptationDecision.reason: Retain with an explicit relation. This is the steering application of rack-and-pinion. The rack rig isolates reversible linear/rotary conversion. Do not dispatch a second car-steering figure under rack-and-pinion. Power assistance is a separate later mechanism.
adaptationDecision.boundary: Catalog and figure metadata establish intended scope only. No existing figure runtime was certified.

prompt.note: Faithful when page 43 is cited for the rack and rods. Changing wheel diameter is an explicit bench comparison. Show wheel pivoting, not wheel rolling, and do not add powered assistance from a different chapter.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Explicit combination of two directly supported diagrams. The exchangeable rims and applied load are comparison fixtures.

teachingAdaptation.assembly: Combines the steering wheel on page 32 with the unassisted steering linkage on page 43.
fixtures: Bench board, crossmember and bearing supports
Two complete exchangeable rims of 30 and 40 cm diameter
Prescribed 100 N external road-wheel resistance represented as rack resistance

actions: Turn left and Turn right prescribe quasi-static steering motion.
Compare wheel sizes exchanges complete rims instantly without changing the column angle or linkage.
teachingAdaptation.idealization: Rigid fixed-length track rods and frictionless geometry; illustrative tooth flanks share a circular pitch with the rack. Does not calculate tyre forces or road dynamics.
